chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ibn Muskān, from Ya'qūb ibn Sālim al-Bazzāz, who said:
Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) said: "Pray them after Fajr,
and recite in them, in the first: 'Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn'
and in the second: 'Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad'.'

key_terms.بَعْدَ الْفَجْرِ: After Fajr (specifically after the call to prayer)
key_terms.صَلِّهِمَا: Pray them (referring to the two units of prayer)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad (Surah Al-Ikhlas, Chapter 112)
key_terms.قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ: Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn (Surah Al-Kafirun, Chapter 109)

ai.seo_question: What surahs should be recited in the two units of the Fajr prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophetic tradition of reciting the 'Qasimayn' (the two halves) surahs in the Fajr prayer, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a Sunnah mu'akkadah. The selection of 'Al-Kafirun' and 'Al-Ikhlas' emphasizes the dual themes of distinct monotheism and the rejection of polytheism, reinforcing the theological core of the morning prayer.
